4_routing_verification.description: Verification that each observed change type routes correctly under the 5 inheritance rules

IR_001.verification_detail: Only ~83 of 2,221 Certified items had content changes in S801-S810. ~2,138 would auto-inherit CertifiedDelta. SHA-256 collision negligible. Normalization ensures whitespace-only changes don't alter hash.

IR_002.detail: S805 (57) + S810 (38) = 95 items with only EW changed. Route to targeted EW review (Gate 2 boilerplate scan). ~3.2 hours saved vs. full re-audit.

IR_003.detail: No pure metadata-only changes in S801-S810. All metadata calibrations co-occurred with content changes.

IR_004.detail: P1-E-056 (S803) CC B->D routes to full re-audit. Sub-type routing (EXPLANATION_ONLY, EW_ONLY, EC_PLUS_EW) verified correct.

IR_005.detail: hash_engine force-clears EW[CC] before hashing. DL-008 is NEVER detected via hash change. IR-005 is the ONLY mechanism preventing DL-008 items from auto-inheriting. Hard dependency on reliable Gate 1 scanning.

4_routing_verification.design_recommendation: Extend spec to handle 'combined change' scenarios where metadata_hash AND content_hash both differ. S810 demonstrated this: all 38 seeds needed both EC review AND difficulty/CL review.

5_reduction_computation.description: Computation of % of certified items that would skip re-review under delta model

conservative_estimate.rationale: If future waves remediate Pack C/D Sections C-F (~250 items) and Pack A B/C/F (~19 items), unchanged count still above 80%.

summary.key_insight: In the 800-series (S801-S810), only 3.7% of certified items had content changes. 96.3% would auto-inherit certification. Item content is dramatically more stable than certification session boundaries imply.
